STEP 1
THE TIME BASED RANGES
What you mark before the open
Time is by far the most important part of my strategy.
Most inconsistent traders I talk to aren't bad at trading.

Most inconsistent traders I talk to aren't bad at trading.

Their timing is just wrong.
And that's actually a good thing.
Fix that one problem, and you only trade at certain times of the day.

No more sitting there for hours
waiting for a pattern to form.

You get in at the same time every single day.

You analyse. You wait for your bias.

See something in that window?
You trade, and you're out fast.

See something in that window?
You trade, and you're out fast.

See nothing?
You don't trade, and you're out fast.
It takes the thinking out of it.

The charts inside that 1 hour window
tell you exactly what to do.

So let's get into what those windows are
and how to mark them.
Now — I've got a number of time based ranges.
Today I'm going to leak 2 of them.

But every single one of them
sits inside a specific dealing range.

So before I give you the times,
I have to show you how I identify a dealing range.

A dealing range is the space between
a significant swing high and a swing low.

And a swing high or a swing low
just means a point where the market turned around.

STEP 2
THE BIAS
Which way you're trading today
So we've got our 2 boxes.

They tell us where the orders are,
and when the market's going to go for them.

What they don't tell us yet
is which way we're trading.
And this is the part everyone assumes is the hard part.
Because you think you have to predict it.

Check the news.
Look at a few higher timeframes.
Form an opinion.

And hope you're right.
Here's what that actually looks like on a normal day.

Market spikes. You buy.
It reverses. Stops you out.

Market spikes. You buy.
It reverses. Stops you out.

So you flip and sell.
And it reverses again.

Anyone done that?

Put it in the chat
Right. All of us.
And that's not a discipline problem.

You're making the biggest decision of your entire day
in the most violent 30 seconds of the session…
…with nothing in front of you to base it on.

Nobody makes a good decision in that state.

Nobody.
So here's the good news.
And this is the part that took the pressure off me completely.
You don't have to predict anything.

Because before this market can make a real move
in either direction, it has to do one thing first.
It has to go and collect the orders sat on one side.

THE ENTRY

1- Has it turned yet?

To know when something stops,
you first have to know what it looks like while it's still going.
SHOW LIVE
d: [Chart in a clear drop. Point at each down-close candle in sequence.]
s:
Down close candle. Then another one lower. Then another one lower.

While a market's falling, every candle keeps closing below the last. That's what falling is.

t: So the turn is when that stops.
SHOW LIVE
d: [Three consecutive down-close candles, then one that closes above all three. Box the three, arrow the fourth.]
s:
Three down close candles — there, there, there.

And then this one closes above all three of them.

One candle just undid three. The thing that was happening has stopped happening.

I call this my three candle rotation. That's delivery being shifted.

t:
Now I want a second opinion,
from a bigger timeframe.
A 5 minute chart can lie to you.
SHOW LIVE
d: [Hourly chart. Three candles. Mark left, middle, right.]
s:
Any 3 hourly candles in a row.

The middle one is the one that dips down and takes the liquidity.

Then the third closes back above the middle.

That's a swing low. The hour agrees.

So if the 9am candle takes the level and the 10am closes back inside… what should the 11am do?

It should go up. And that's exactly what it does.

t:
That's the 3 candle swing structure.

It's confirmation for your direction.
It is not where you buy.

It is not where you buy.

It's what tells you buying is worth doing.

If you treat your hourly candles as your daily candles,
a whole new world opens up.

Knowing it's turned still isn't a price.

Why this one? Because this is the candle that traded into the liquidity below the low — and then we closed back above it.

That's the candle that took everyone's stops. The one the algorithm used to do the job.

So its body is my level. And here's what people get wrong:

I don't buy when it closes. I buy when price comes back to it.

Watch. It comes back into it. And it doesn't carry on. It stops.

Past 25 — sentiment's beginning to shift, buyers are stepping in. That's my confirmation.

Past 50 — the market has no need to return back to 25. That's where I move to break even.

50 to 75 — that's where I'm taking money off.

And once it closes at 75, that's exactly where it should rally into the opposing end.

t: 3- Take the money and get out.
